decision.detail: I pull my coat off the hook by the booth door. I walk past the station line, past the tape still warm on the patch, past the click of the open switchboard. I walk into the ballroom. The lights are low and gold. Someone is already moving. I find a chair near the wall, set my notebook on the seat beside me, and I stand. I do not open the notebook. I do not write. I watch the floor. I listen to the music, which is old, which is slow, which is the kind of record a man like Alma would have wound onto a reel and played for no one but the machinery. I let the evening pass through me. I do not dance. I do not talk to anyone. I stand by the wall and I let the room be a room and not a set and not a story. I leave before the last song.
decision.intention: Not record. Not cover. Not transmit. Let the tape sit on the patch where it is. Let the line stay open for whoever needs it. Let the ballroom be a ballroom for one more evening. I am not the woman who sends the voice to Pittsburgh tonight. Larry has his reel. Phil has his nod. The crew has their cameras. I have my evening. One evening where I am not a producer, not a piece, not a promise. I am a woman standing by a wall in a room that is about to go dark, listening to a song I know, doing nothing that will end up in an edit.

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
